source.title: Solution space and storage capacity of fully connected two-layer neural networks with generic activation functions

record.tranche_reason: The study measures how well gradient-trained fully connected networks find solutions for random input-output labels, using a different setup from the versions’ natural-data generalization comparisons.
record.gate_note: The numerical experiment uses random inputs and random labels and reports training loss and estimated storage capacity. It does not measure held-out performance or natural-label generalization. The paper’s mentions of generalization and double descent are background or future directions.
record.test_reason: The study measures storage capacity on random Gaussian inputs and random binary labels. It reports no natural-label or held-out performance, so it does not test V1's coexistence of memorization and generalization. Generalization and double descent appear as background and future directions; none of V2–V8 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Under the stated activation assumptions, the heuristic replica analysis predicts finite storage capacity per parameter at infinite width. Numerical training finds lower capacities than the 1-RSB predictions; the authors attribute this gap to nonconvexity and trapping in local minima. They also report negative hidden-weight correlations consistent with division of labor.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes a fully connected two-layer network on random Gaussian inputs and random binary labels, with fixed output weights, norm-constrained hidden weights, hinge loss, and Adam. It does not compare natural-label test error with random-label test error.
record.method_sensitivity: For erf, the loss behavior differs across N/K values; N/K = 50 is described as closest to the replica-analysis setting. For ReLU, the reported loss increase is consistent across tested N/K values.

fits_no_version.finding: With 10,000 hidden-weight parameters, Adam training yields estimated random-data storage capacities of approximately 2.5 pairs per parameter for ReLU and 3.8 for erf at N/K = 50. These estimates concern fitting training data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation choice affects the random-data storage capacity accessible to gradient training in constrained two-layer fully connected networks.

record.peer_reviewed: Journal of the Physical Society of Japan
record.problems: The replica calculation is explicitly described as heuristic rather than rigorous. Numerical experiments use finite parameter count and 10 datasets per combination; the authors say they do not measure the replica overlaps q and d because of limited computational resources.

untested.parts: Whether the same architectures and training recipes generalize on natural labels while fitting random labels, and whether random-label held-out accuracy remains at chance.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the width needed to interpolate.
Convolutional versus fully connected image generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus nonadaptive optimizer held-out performance under different tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to generalization gaps.
Test-accuracy effects of removing memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: Finite storage capacity and failure to find solutions at larger dataset-to-parameter ratios do not challenge any listed generalization version. No verdict labels apply.

versions.untested_parts: The study examines training on random labels, but does not test natural-label training, held-out accuracy, or whether held-out accuracy on random labels stays at chance.
No test-error sweep over widths beyond the interpolation threshold.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks on images.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out performance.
No measurement of sharpness or other generalization-gap measures.
No removal of memorized examples or test-accuracy comparison.

rows.subject: FCM with ReLU activations
rows.operation_detail: Trained on random input-output datasets using hinge loss and Adam; estimated experimental storage capacity from the increase in loss.

conditions.value: terminated below 10−5 loss or at 5000 epochs

rows.measure: Estimated experimental storage capacity for random input-output pairs per parameter
rows.note: The authors report the estimate consistently across the tested N/K values. This is a training-capacity result, not a held-out generalization result.
rows.check: The approximately 2.5 random pairs per parameter capacity estimate matches Section 3.2, but training capacity alone cannot establish V1's coexistence claim.

rows.operation_detail: Trained on random input-output datasets using hinge loss and Adam; estimated experimental storage capacity from the training loss.

conditions.value: terminated below 10−5 loss or at 5000 epochs

rows.measure: Estimated experimental storage capacity for random input-output pairs per parameter
rows.note: The text says loss behavior differs across N/K values and identifies N/K = 50 as closest to the replica-analysis setting. This is a training-capacity result, not a held-out generalization result.
rows.check: The approximately 3.8 capacity estimate for erf at N/K = 50 matches Section 3.2, but it measures training capacity without natural-label or held-out performance.
